_notes: The lamps are lit in the wrong order and the Lamplighters are nowhere. The rag-wraith is the lesson about declining a fight.
Scenes 12-17 of the prologue as it was before the split; `--scene story:<index>` still counts across the whole prologue, not within this file.

lines: That was when I noticed the quiet. No pigeons.
Understand: pigeons are never quiet. The roosts over Needle Lane keep up a session of complaint and scandal from dusk to dawn, and I have slept under that noise my whole life.
It was not there. The roofline sat against the sky, empty as a shelf.
The lamps on Needle Lane are lit in the wrong order.

You would have to live here to see it. Third lamp, then first, then the one by the pump. The order is the point — I have heard a lamplighter say so on a doorstep to an apprentice: we light them in an order, lad, and the order is the stitch.
Tonight the lane reads dark-bright-dark-dark-bright. A signature forged by someone who has only ever seen it written.
The dog at Number Twelve is awake — I can smell him being awake — and he does not bark, which he has never once in his loud and tedious life failed to do.
And halfway down, the fog stops being fog. It has sleeves. It has a collar. It has the shape of a person who is not in it.
Every cut thread on this street is sliding towards it like water finding a drain, and the shape is gathering them in. It turns what it has instead of a face towards me.

notes: ❋ GUILE, the green patience — and MOONLIGHT, which is hers. Moonlight is WILD: one Moonlight card pays for anything you own.

coach.text: Nothing was healed on the walk here. Your heart, your spool and every action's remaining uses carried straight over from the wisp — one night, one budget, all the way to the end of it.
A RAG-WRAITH: clothes whose owner is missing. Not dead — missing. It is above your weight, and it knows it. Ten years ago it would still have been above your weight.
Guile in hand, which is what the LOAF wants: block 5, but it costs your whole turn. A loaf is not a lunge.
PURR heals 2 a turn for two turns — but Ash lies still while it lasts, and it breaks the moment you are hit. Purr behind a guard, never in the open.
CONCENTRATE, for an empty hand: give up the turn to will one spent energy back. It arrives NEXT turn. Twice a fight.
And you do not have to win this. SLIP AWAY is a real answer — though it gets its telegraphed move in as you go.

lines: I went in with everything I had left, and then with the thing of hers I carry, the pale cold weight under my ribs that is not mine and never was. I felt it go out of me and do nothing.
Then I did the intelligent thing, which the stories never put in. Three streets before I stopped, and I stopped because my legs decided it, not me.
And yet. It was not hunting me. All that gathered-up stolen thread, and it spent none of it on a cat. It was WORKING, and I did not know yet at what.
It comes apart in the middle of the road, and the threads it was pulling go slack.
That was above my weight and both of us knew it. I do not feel clever. I feel like something let go.
It was not hunting me. It was WORKING, and I did not know yet at what.
